summary: Kendall R. Marchman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied under Mario Poceski and completed his PhD at the University of Florida in 2015.

Kengo Harimoto specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyushu University and earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Wilhelm Halbfass in 1999. He later held posts at Mahidol University and the University of Naples "L'Orientale."

Kenichi Kuranishi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held appointments as an associate professor at Taisho University (attested 2013–2026) and as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).
Kenji Ishii is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1973 to 1983. He served on the faculty at Kokugakuin University from circa 1996 to 2020.
Kenji Kinugawa specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1971 to 1979 under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.

Kenji Matsuo is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1975 to 1985 and held a post at Yamagata University from circa 1987 to 2020.

Kenji Shimada (1917–2000) was a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and history who studied at Kyoto University (~1938–1941). He held positions at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities (~1949–1973) and as a researcher at Kyoto University (~1973–1981).

Kenji Takahashi specializes in Indology. He studied at Leiden University (2015–2016) and under Diwakar Acharya, Yuko Yokochi, and Peter C. Bisschop, later holding a JSPS-sponsored fellowship at the University of Naples Federico II from 2019 to 2021.
Kenji Watanabe works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jozef Deleu and held a post as an assistant at Taisho University in 1978.
Kenjiu Kasawara (1851–1883) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Oxford in 1879 and was taught by Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell.
Kenjuro Yanagida (1893–1983) was a philosopher who studied at Yokohama National University and under Kitaro Nishida (~1922–1925). He held a post at Hirosaki University circa 1949–1950.
Kenkai Naganuma (1883–1980) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He served as professor emeritus at Kyushu University (~1946–1980) and held an appointment at Kurume University.
Kennard Lipman specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies under Herbert V. Guenther and worked as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.
Kenneth Doo Young Lee works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University under Ryuichi Abe and held a post at Stetson University in 2007.

Kenneth G. Zysk is an Indologist and historian educated at UC Santa Barbara and the Australian National University. He held posts at UCLA, Wisconsin-Madison, Toronto, Eastern Michigan University, and the University of Copenhagen (attested 2012–2026).

Kenneth J. Guest is a scholar of religious studies and sinology. He studied at Columbia, Union Theological Seminary, Peking University, and the CUNY Graduate Center, and held teaching posts at Hunter College and Baruch College.

Kenneth J. Saunders (1883–1937) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under W. D. C. Wagiswara (~1908–1912). He served as a lecturer at the University of California and professor at the Pacific School of Religion (~1921–1935).

Kenneth K. Inada (1923–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was a professor at the University at Buffalo (attested 1983–1999) and served as chair at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research from 1996 to 1999.

Kenneth K. Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and served as a professor and director at Musashino University between 1998 and 2014.
Kenneth R. Valpey specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and held a post at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
